comments.text: Blocking: R10 bundles three behaviours: responsive scaling, code-only graphics/sound, and a mute toggle. Split them so each can be implemented and accepted on its own. A10 then checks scaling and mute but not code-generated assets, which belongs with R1.

text: R5: WHEN the cat touches a fish treat, the system SHALL add 10 points to the score and remove the treat.
prefix: take one of the cat's 3 lives.
suffix: R6: WHEN the cat loses its last

comments.text: Blocking: No requirement says how fish treats appear (spawn, position, rate, lifetime, or what happens when one is missed). A5 can only be tested if a treat already exists. Add a requirement for fish spawning.
This is template boilerplate and does not apply to a game with no beans. Remove it and describe the three states and their elements only.

R4 bundles four effects (remove cucumber, lose a life, show a bubble, play a sound). Consider splitting at least the feedback (bubble and sound) from the life loss. Also state the speech bubble duration, and whether the cat has brief invulnerability after a hit, so overlapping cucumbers do not take several lives at once.
R3 does not say how rate and speed grow or cap, so the game can become impossible. State a maximum, or at least require that a path to dodge always exists.

text: R8: WHEN the player presses P or Escape, or the tab loses focus, while the game is running, the system SHALL pause it; pressing the same key SHALL resume it.

comments.text: After a tab focus loss there is no 'same key' to resume with, so the resume trigger is undefined. State how play resumes (for example on P or Escape, or on a tap). A8 then needs a matching check for resuming after focus loss.
